_comment: The parity query list. Both src-tauri/examples/gen_query_golden.rs and
internal/dbcore's tests read THIS file, so neither side can drift onto a
different statement. Each case names the fixture targets it applies to.
'mysql' and 'mariadb' are separate targets even though both use the
SupportedDB 'mariadb' tag, because the two servers decode differently.
A case with a 'table' models the table-scoped get_rows path, where the backend can look up column metadata. Cases without one model arbitrary console SQL, where it cannot.

cases.name: hazards-all
cases.why: every decoding hazard at once: numeric precision, boolean vs int, zoned vs naive timestamps, json, bytes, geometry, nulls
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: count-star
cases.why: MySQL returns COUNT(*) as BIGINT UNSIGNED; it must not surface as a string or a bool

cases.name: duplicate-column-labels
cases.why: unique_col_name: a join exposing id and label twice must yield id, label, id_1, label_1 in that order
cases.sql: SELECT p.a AS id, p.label, c.id, c.pa AS label FROM parent p JOIN child c ON c.pa = p.a ORDER BY p.a

cases.name: boolean-vs-integer
cases.why: the is_boolean_column rule in isolation: one declared boolean, one integer holding the same 0/1
cases.sql: SELECT id, is_true, int_not_bool FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: numeric-precision
cases.why: a numeric that loses digits if it is routed through a float must arrive as a string
cases.sql: SELECT id, exact_money, big_int FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: expression-labels
cases.why: computed columns with no table behind them, plus a NULL literal
cases.sql: SELECT 1 AS one, 'txt' AS s, NULL AS nothing_at_all

cases.name: pg-arrays
cases.why: Postgres text[] and bigint[] decode to JSON arrays, not to strings
cases.sql: SELECT id, tags, nums FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: pg-geometry
cases.why: PostGIS geometry and geography have no driver type; they must fall through to uppercase hex, never to null
cases.sql: SELECT id, geom, geog FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: pg-enum-uuid-json
cases.why: enum, uuid and jsonb each take a distinct branch of the decode chain
cases.sql: SELECT id, feeling, ident, doc FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: pg-schema-qualified
cases.why: a table outside the public schema
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM extra.elsewhere ORDER BY id

cases.name: my-unsigned-and-geometry
cases.why: BIGINT UNSIGNED above i64::MAX, plus MySQL Spatial geometry falling through to hex
cases.sql: SELECT id, ubig_int, geom, blob_col FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: my-enum-json
cases.why: MySQL enum arrives as a string and json as a parsed value
cases.sql: SELECT id, feeling, doc FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: sqlite-affinity
cases.why: SQLite stores whatever it was given; the declared type is all the decoder has to go on
cases.sql: SELECT id, exact_money, real_num, dt_naive, d, raw, geom FROM hazards ORDER BY id

cases.name: empty-result
cases.why: a zero-row result must be an empty array, not null

cases.name: timestamp-precision
cases.why: chrono to_rfc3339 writes +00:00 and auto-sizes the fraction to 0/3/6/9 places; Go's time.RFC3339 writes Z and trims. Both differences are invisible without this case.
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM ts_precision ORDER BY id
